children: Asian currencies are likely to be the "defensive" against the dollar, MUFG Bank's Lloyd Chan says in a research report. Markets have continued to "price a more prolonged Fed tightening cycle," the senior currency analyst says. "The absence of any pushback [from Warsh] against recent Fed repricing leaves elevated U.S. yields and the resilient dollar as key headwinds for regional currencies," Chan says. The analyst notes Fed Chair Warsh on Monday steered clear of near-term policy outlook, focusing instead on uncertain impact of artificial intelligence on productivity, employment, and financial markets. The U.S. dollar edges 0.1% higher to 159.53 yen and is 0.4% higher at 1,340.50 won while the Australian dollar is little changed at US$0.6735, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
